newsitem.title: DENMARK: Profit-taking puts soaring Danish shares into dive.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking puts soaring Danish shares into dive.

text.p: Profit-taking stopped Danish share prices setting a record for the second consecutive day on Wednesday and dealers saw little chance of significant gains on Thursday.
"It's been a day marked by profit-taking and that's typical, every time we hit the top we fall back directly afterward," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index fell 0.81 point to 120.93, in overall bourse turnover of 1.1 billion crowns, after earlier peaking at 121.88. The KFX September future fell 0.35 point to 121.10 with 235 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
As in Tuesday's record-breaking trade, the focus was largely upon banks and insurance companies.
Unidanmark rose three crowns to 270 crowns but Den Danske Bank fell by the same amount to 424 crowns. More than 250,000 shares in each were traded, dealers said.
Insurer Top Danmark rose 14 crowns to 670 crowns and one dealer surmised that Unidanmark's stated intention to increase its insurance activity was a factor in the banking group's rise.
"Suddenly there's interest in the finance industry, particularly insurance," the dealer said.
